# LLMHarbor — full site content

## Home (https://llmharbor.vercel.app/)

**LLMHarbor: one OpenAI-compatible API for 1,313 free model endpoints**

LLMHarbor routes every request across 87 free LLM providers and 1,313 free model endpoints behind one OpenAI-compatible /v1 API — encrypted keys, per-key budgets, automatic failover. Free and open source.

### Hero

Free LLMs, one API. LLMHarbor puts the free tiers of 87 LLM providers — 1,313 model endpoints and 10.1 billion tokens a month — behind one OpenAI-compatible /v1 endpoint. You keep one key, one base URL and one bill of zero. Open source, MIT licensed, self-host it anywhere.

### What it does

- **Picks the best model**: every request is routed to the fastest model that can serve it, chosen from your ordered fallback chain. This week: 62% of requests go to the first choice, 31% to the second, 7% to the fallback.
- **Falls over on rate limits**: when a provider throttles or hits its cap, the next provider takes the request before your caller ever sees it.
- **Keeps keys encrypted**: provider keys are encrypted at rest; clients only ever see one unified key minted in the dashboard.
- **Counts tokens per key**: usage is tracked per key against every provider's free-tier cap, so you never quietly pass a limit.

### Windows 7 x86

Every screenshot on the site was taken on a stock Windows 7 x86 machine — Windows 7 x86 SP1, 2 GB DDR2 RAM, Intel(R) Atom(TM) CPU N280 @ 1.66GHz (1.33GHz), and an HDD (70GB ST9160310AS ATA Device) — to show LLMHarbor performs well on legacy hardware. The same router runs on a modern server and on a phone; it does not demand a new one. Windows 7 SP1 users take the portable zip from the dedicated release, since the latest .exe will not run there.

### Provider hub

87 free LLM providers, 1,313 free model endpoints, behind one base URL. The router holds them all in one catalog and serves them through the same /v1 surface: chat completions, embeddings, image generation, audio, plus an MCP server.

## Dashboard (https://llmharbor.vercel.app/dashboard.html)

Every request, routed and counted. The models list on the left is every endpoint the router can reach; the open item on the right is this month's usage — tokens spent per key, against the free-tier cap of each provider. Tokens this month: 7.4B of the 10.1B free tier. The page also carries the full Windows 7 x86 showcase: all six real screenshots and the machine they were taken on (Windows 7 x86 SP1, 2 GB DDR2 RAM, Intel Atom N280 @ 1.66GHz, 70GB ST9160310AS HDD).

## Features (https://llmharbor.vercel.app/features.html)

The router does four jobs: picks the best model, fails over on rate limits, keeps keys encrypted, and counts tokens per key. Four jobs that turn free-tier keys into one dependable endpoint.

## Providers (https://llmharbor.vercel.app/providers.html)

One endpoint, every provider. The router holds the free tiers of 87 providers in one catalog and serves them through the same /v1 surface: chat, embeddings, images, audio and an MCP server. Every endpoint family is OpenAI-compatible, so existing OpenAI SDK code works unchanged.

## How to start (https://llmharbor.vercel.app/how.html)

Three steps: pick a model from the 1,313 free endpoints, add your free provider keys (encrypted at rest), and point your client at one base URL — http://localhost:3001/v1. Point any OpenAI-compatible client at that URL with the unified key from the dashboard and send requests as usual.

## Download (https://llmharbor.vercel.app/download.html)

Pick the release that matches your device. Windows 7 SP1 users must take the portable zip — the latest .exe will not run there. Release links by audience:

- **Windows 7 SP1** → portable zip: https://github.com/Zelvior-Labs/llmharbor/releases#release-win7-v0.16.34-preview.1
- **Android 8.0+ (armeabi-v7a, armeabi-v8a)** → .apk: https://github.com/Zelvior-Labs/llmharbor/releases#release-android-v0.16.34-preview.3 (recommended — works on both legacy and modern)
- **Android 11+ (armeabi-v7a, armeabi-v8a)** → .apk: https://github.com/Zelvior-Labs/llmharbor/releases#release-android-v0.16.34-preview.2
- **Android 11 (armeabi-v7a)** → .apk: https://github.com/Zelvior-Labs/llmharbor/releases#release-android-v0.16.34-preview.1
